answer: A Sybil-resistant registry forces every agent to lock a stake before it may vote. Think of the stake as a seed planted in a shared garden: to run thousands of fake identities an attacker must post thousands of independent bonds, and the required deposit rises quadratically with each new alias. Random audits slash the whole hoard when forgery is found, whether the swarm arrives like a comet or drifts in as a zephyr of throwaway accounts. Since audits are unpredictable, the expected penalty outweighs any vote gain.
